text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- The Paris conference on Bosnia represents an important step in the implementation of the peace agreement -- especially its civilian part, says Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic.
- Yugoslav and Croatian Interior Ministers will meet in Belgrade Friday to discuss liberalisation of visa and travel regimes.
- The Yugoslav government approves opening of Russian consulate in Montenegro's capital of Podgorica.
- Mira Markovic, member of the directorate of the Yugoslav left (JUL) and wife of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic promotes her book Odgovor (Response) in Slovenia.
- Delegation of the British "Know-How" fund talks with a Yugoslav parliamentary delegation on extending technical aid to Yugoslavia to develope capital markets.
- Taxi drivers and lawyers protesting over taxes again even though tax rates have been halved.
- Yugoslav insurance companies have on the whole been successful in the first half of the year. Fourty out of 59 companies registered a positive balance and earned 12 million dinars.

- The nation's Agricultural machinery is outdated and needs to be renewed. Parities for purchase of agricultural machines will be esataablished by the end of year, says representative of the Yugoslav agriculture ministry.
- Yugoslav company Aviogeneks sold two 732-200 Boeing aircraft to an unknown buyer. The planes flew to El Salvador.
- Yugoslav agricultural machine producers prepare to export machines to China worth $31.5 million within the scope of the Yugoslav-Chinese barter deals.
- Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic says the federation will participate in the financing of the economy of Kragujevac and especially of the Zastava industrial group.
